recipes.name: Burgundy Pork Tenderloin
ingredients_raw: 1 (.75 ounce) packet dry brown gravy mix

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Place pork in a 9x13 inch baking dish, and sprinkle meat with salt, pepper and garlic powder. Top with onion and celery, and pour wine over all.
Bake in the preheated oven for 45 minutes.

When done baking, remove meat from baking dish, and place on a serving platter. Pour gravy mix into baking dish with wine and cooking juices, and stir until thickened. Slice meat, and cover with the gravy.

raw_recipe.headline: Burgundy Pork Tenderloin
raw_recipe.description: Impress your guests with a pork tenderloin, lightly seasoned and baked, and served with the simple red wine sauce that cooks along with the pork. All you have to do is smile and accept the compliments.

video.description: See how to make pork tenderloin that's served with a rich red wine sauce. So easy to prepare, the wine sauce cooks right along with the roasting meat. It's foolproof!

review.reviewBody:
This recipe is great, and making it is about as easy as falling off a log. You need to know some things though, so yours will turn out wonderfully, like mine does every time i make this recipe. 
First of all, the pork should be relatively pink when it is done. This is due to the fact that it was swimming in Burgundy Red Wine. Be sure to use a meat thermometer and bring the temp to 160, and if any of your guests complains that they think they are going to get trichanosis, politely ask them to leave and go to applebees where they process and overcook everything. 
Next, I am not sure how this recipe was called Burgundy Pork Tenderloin and it calls for red wine. Be sure to use BURGUNDY red wine, as the title suggests. The fun thing about burgundy is that there is no such thing as an expensive burgundy wine. It is usuall near the mogen david and other cheap wines. Don't bother changing the Bbrown gravy amount. Also, the first time I made this I thought I would be smart and braise the roast first to make it more tender. The next time I made it I just threw all the ingredient into the pan as the recipe suggests and it came out way better. It takes about five minutes to construct this recipe and it is the best I have ever found. 
Have fun!

Simple recipe but changed it a bit. No onion or celery. Instead I added onion powder, chili powder and Cayenne pepper on the pork. Placed the seasoned pork in fridge for 1 hour.
A little Olive oil in high skillet, quickly fry some red and green bell peppers, removed it. Add the pork loin, and sear 30 seconds each side. Now add 1 cup red wine, 1 cup beef broth, the bell peppers, and sprinkle the pork with thyme and rosemary. Simmer for about 30-40 minutes (internal temp 165 degrees)
Remove pork, strain the sauce and put in saucepan. Add a bit more red wine, melt some butter in it, add a shot of heavy cream and a spoon of all purpose flour. heat for 2 minutes while mixing and you have an amazing sauce that goes perfect with the flavorful and spiced pork loin.

I have never written a review for all recipes before but felt this recipe warranted one. I was pleasantly surprised by how delicious this simple meal turned out, and I am a self-proclaimed foodie:) Like others, I did change the recipe a bit, based on my own tastes. After seasoning the pork with salt, pepper and minced garlic, I browned both sides. I then placed the meat in a baking dish, covered with some precut veggies I bought at Kroger - squash, onions, zucchini and carrots, mixed 1 cup of merlot with 1 cup beef consumme (Campbells), and poured that on top. I cooked the meat for 45 min but probably would decrease to 40 min next time. I then poured the wine-consumme mixture into a pan, mixed in some corn starch blended with water, and brought to a boil. I then simmered for a few minutes to desired thickness and served over the meat and precut veggies. Some fresh thyme might be a nice touch next time too. Excellent restaurant-quality meal. I would highly recommend!

The timing on the meat and the ratio of liquid to meat was spot on so the meat came out tender and juicy. However, the red wine turned the surface an unappetizing purple. Likewise, the predominance of red wine in the gravy made it harsh, even though I used a good bottle. After removing the cooked meat, I gave the gravy a more meaty and complex taste (and a thicker texture) by adding 2 tbsps of butter, a pinch of dried thyme, 2 pinches of sugar, a teaspoon of corn starch, and a beef bouillon cube (Knorrs). I then cut the meat in thick slices and let it sit in the warm, thickened gravy before serving. In the future I would sear the meat before putting it in the cooking liquid, omit the gravy mix and change the 2 cups of cooking liquid to 75% broth and 25% wine. I would also add some bay leaf or thyme to the cooking liquid in order to impart a little herbal taste.

Followed others’ suggestions and browned the pork loin for a few minutes on each side. Omitted the celery. Sautéed the onions and sliced mushrooms before topping the pork with them. Replaced 1 cup of beef consommé for 1 of the cups of wine. Also used two packets of brown gravy mix instead of one. Loved it!
Changed to 1 cup wine and 1 cup beef broth as suggested. Also moved the sauce to a pan and simmered down to thicken. Great recipe!

I couldn't believe how great it was for being so easy to pull together. I used salt, pepper, garlic powder to season my meat, then in EVOO I seared/browned my pork in a cast iron pan for about 12 minutes all around. (we like the taste and appearance of browned carmelized meat) Used 1 cup of pinot noir (nothing fancy) and 1 cup beef broth. I'm a big wine lover but felt 2 cups of wine would be too strong a wine flavor to the gravy. Put the same pan into the oven. I used one packet of McCormick Brown Gravy mix. I did not use the sliced onion or celery as I didn't think they'd really contribute much to the flavor. The whole family loved it. Definite keeper.

Wow! I didn’t have any red wine handy, so I substituted one cup reduced sodium beef broth and one cup water. (I didn’t use all beef broth for the liquid because I didn’t want the gravy to be too salty.) I also chose a reduced sodium brown gravy mix. Other than that, I stuck to the recipe even though cooking meat in liquid has sometimes been a negative experience for me. I couldn’t be more pleased with the outcome. The meat was juicy and tender. Be sure to let the meat rest five or ten minutes before cutting or the juices will run out. Since we love veggies, I didn’t strain the broth before making the gravy, and everyone was pleased with the meat and the sauce.

We loved this recipe. I seared the pork tenderloin before roasting, gave it a nice caramel color. I also used 1 cup of beef broth and a half cup of burgundy wine for the sauce. I like having the onions and celery in the sauce. I think next time I will double the sauce. I had to cook my tenderloins about 10 minutes longer than called for because the were a little larger. We had plenty of leftovers so I chopped it up and added it to cooked egg noodles to make a pork noodle dish. That's why I would double the sauce next time. This is going in my permanent recipe collection.

Left out the veggies, seasoned with salt, pepper, garlic and onion powder. I only made a one-pound tenderloin, so cut most ingredients in half. Still didn't need a full cup of wine. I added beef broth and half a packet of (mushroom) gravy mix. Seared the meat first, then baked for 25-30 mins. It was very good. The fam loved it.

Used fresh sliced mushrooms as my mother cannot tolerate onions. I added the gravy mix to my wine and sat it on top of the stove, stirring.thinking, “ when is is this stuff supposed to thicken?” I put the burner on high heat and placed the chops back in the pan while I was doing that too, seemed like they weren’t quite done from when they were in the oven. Came out quite well, nice flavor from that wine bath. I used just over two cups. Turned out that was just about the whole bottle of (cooking) wine.
Fantastic flavors, everyone loved it.
Loved the recipe. Only changed the gravy, thicken with cornstarch. It was delicious.
I reduced the red wine to 1 1/2 cups.

Delicious!! 4.5 stars but I will round up because this couldn’t be an easier, amazing weeknight meal! I thought the celery was a bit odd so I subbed some sliced mushrooms instead. Adding the gravy mix and stirring never really thickened to a “gravy” consistency but was still good. Added the sliced pork back just before bringing to the table. Served with instant mashed potatoes (Remember! Busy weeknight!!) and a side of green beans. We couldn’t be happier and I will make again! Thank you Kathleen!
No changes. Delicious as is.
Surprising good for how easy it was to prepare! I subbed masala for burgundy, no celery, 1 cup wine and 1 cup chicken stock, made my own mix. The gravy was excellent on the entire meal. Yummy!

I covered the pork while baking and ended up with soooo much red wine that the brown gravy mix did nothing but make soup! I added 3 HUGE tablespoons of flour to get a gravy consistency, but the red wine was overpowering.
Definitely need to reduce wine by half. Having to now make a roux just to make some gravy....
Veggies didn't cook enough or blend in with the wine while cooking. Lots of questions about this recipe...
